agent_assessment: Research conclusion is well-grounded: all factual codebase claims (livedesktop package contents, procmetrics location, iframe-bridge package, deployment-manager external-url pattern, smoketest xvfb-run usage) were verified against the working tree. All 9 follow-up backlog items described in the conclusion's Actions section were created with correct kinds, priorities, efforts, dependencies, acceptance_allow scopes, and initiative assignment. Dependency graph is internally consistent and matches the phased hard-cut strategy in Finding 15. Three pre-existing overlapping items (vrooli-emulator-linux-first, adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows, vrooli-emulator-remote-node-backend) were intentionally not duplicated; notes.md flags these for human reconciliation. One inconsistency worth noting: the research spec.json status field is 'failed' despite the conclusion and notes.md describing a successful completion — likely an artifact of an unsatisfied upstream dependency marker rather than a content issue.
notes: Research item spec.json has status='failed' but the conclusion.md is complete, notes.md documents successful follow-up batch-create, and all 9 actions landed as described. Likely caused by unsatisfied depends_on markers (qa-scenario-to-desktop-code-quality-20260407, qa-prompt-manager-* items) rather than research failure — worth verifying during archive decision.

Conclusion Finding 9 describes deployment-manager's embed pattern as 'GET /embedded/{name}/external-url' (parameterized). Actual usage in deployment-manager/ui/src/pages/Analyze.tsx:47 hits '/embedded/scenario-dependency-analyzer/external-url' — a concrete path, not a template. Close enough for planning purposes; phase 2 implementers should confirm the exact backend contract before copying the pattern.

Pre-existing items execute/vrooli-emulator-linux-first (XL umbrella), execute/adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows, and execute/vrooli-emulator-remote-node-backend overlap in scope with the newly-created items. notes.md explicitly defers reconciliation to a human; archive decision should factor in whether to close/retarget these before the emulator-platform initiative starts executing.

acceptance_allow for execute/smoketest-delegate-display-to-emulator spans TWO scenarios (scenario-to-desktop + vrooli-emulator). Cross-scenario acceptance scopes are unusual in this backlog but matches the conclusion's intent: smoketest changes on the consumer side and emulator client code on the provider side must land together.

execute/scaffold-vrooli-emulator-scenario is effort=L with a broad description (API scaffold + livedesktop move + procmetrics move + route prefix change + headless flag + CLI surface + drop GET artifact). Workshopping should consider splitting scaffolding from the internal-package migrations to reduce single-change blast radius — but that's a planning concern for the execute item, not a blocker for archiving the research.

evidence.title: Research spec status is 'failed' despite successful completion
evidence.description: spec.json at research/emulator-extraction-and-service-plan/spec.json reports status='failed' (line 19). However conclusion.md is complete, notes.md documents successful 9-item batch-create, and all 9 follow-up items exist with the correct dependency link back to this research item. The 'failed' status is likely a stale marker from unsatisfied upstream dependencies (depends_on includes two qa-prompt-manager-* items and qa-scenario-to-desktop-code-quality-* that show as deleted in git status) rather than actual research failure. Reviewer should confirm whether the final status should be flipped before archive.

improvement_suggestions.description: Add an automated consistency check in swarm-manager backlog tooling that compares a research item's conclusion.md 'Actions' count against the number of depends_on→research links pointing back from child items. Would catch cases where a conclusion declares N actions but fewer than N follow-up items were created (or items exist but don't link back).

Research-item review rounds currently have to manually grep the codebase to verify that Findings quote real files/paths. Consider a lightweight 'finding-citation' check: if a conclusion.md mentions a concrete file path (e.g. 'api/livedesktop/service.go:289'), the review tool could auto-verify existence and flag broken references.

spec.json status='failed' on a research item whose conclusion.md and notes.md both indicate success suggests the depends_on resolution check is run at item creation time but not re-evaluated when upstream dependencies are completed or removed. A periodic reconciliation (or an event hook when depends_on items change state) would keep the status field truthful.
